verses.text: Now after the Sabbath, as it began to dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
Behold, there was a great earthquake, for an angel of the Lord descended from the sky, and came and rolled away the stone from the door, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
For fear of him, the guards shook, and became like dead men.
The angel answered the women, “Don’t be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus, who has been crucified.
He is not here, for he has risen, just like he said. Come, see the place where the Lord was lying.
Go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and behold, he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Behold, I have told you.”
They departed quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring his disciples word.

As they went to tell his disciples, behold, Jesus met them, saying,
“Rejoice!”
They came and took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.

Then Jesus said to them,
“Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers

that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
Now while they were going, behold, some of the guards came into the city, and told the chief priests all the things that had happened.
When they were assembled with the elders, and had taken counsel, they gave a large amount of silver to the soldiers,
saying, “Say that his disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.
If this comes to the governor’s ears, we will persuade him and make you free of worry.”
So they took the money and did as they were told. This saying was spread abroad among the Jews, and continues until today.
But the eleven disciples went into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had sent them.
When they saw him, they bowed down to him, but some doubted.

Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying,
“All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.

Go
and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

items.label: M1
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: The teller sets the time as just after the Sabbath, at dawn on the week's first day.
items.gloss: Time is set by the Sabbath and the count of days — the event is placed inside Israel's sacred week, not on a neutral calendar.
items.sitz: a Judean teller placing an event by Sabbath-reckoning and day-count

items.label: M2
items.agent: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary
items.outcome: the two women arrive at the tomb
items.paraphrase: The two Marys go to the tomb to look at it.
items.gloss: What follows now rests on what these women saw and can vouch for; the account leans on human witness at the grave.
items.sitz: women visiting a fresh burial site at first light

items.label: M3
items.outcome: a great earthquake occurs
items.paraphrase: The ground shakes violently.
items.gloss: The shaking ground signals that God himself is acting here — the earth registers a heavenly intervention, not just a natural tremor.
items.sitz: a portent-quake at a numinous moment

lineage.seam: Is MATT-28-WEB standing on Exodus 19:18 here — and if so, what shifts? (reuses the Sinai-theophany earthquake as the ground-signal of divine

items.label: M4
items.outcome: the angel arrives at the tomb site
items.paraphrase: An angel of the Lord comes down out of the sky.
items.gloss: A figure from the heavenly court crosses down into the human scene, opening the ordinary world to what lies above it.
items.sitz: a messenger from the heavenly court arriving on earth

lineage.seam: imports the Danielic angelophany-vocabulary (face-like-lightning, garments of dazzling brightness) as the visual signature of the tomb-messe

items.label: M5
items.outcome: the tomb is opened
items.paraphrase: The angel rolls the stone away from the tomb door.
items.gloss: The sealed grave is opened from the outside by heaven's hand; the barrier between the dead and the living is unmade for the reader before anything else is said.
items.sitz: opening a sealed rock-cut grave

items.label: M6
items.outcome: the angel is enthroned on the stone
items.paraphrase: The angel sits down on the rolled-away stone.
items.gloss: By sitting on the very stone that once sealed the tomb, the messenger takes an authoritative seat over the defeated barrier — death is now something to sit upon.
items.sitz: a messenger taking a seated posture of authority at the opened grave

items.label: M7
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: The angel looks like lightning and is dressed in snow-white clothing.
items.gloss: The teller reaches for lightning and snow because ordinary description won't hold the figure; the imagery signals a reality that plain speech can only gesture at.
items.sitz: witness-report of a dazzling heavenly figure

lineage.seam: borrows the 'garment white as snow' register from the Ancient-of-Days theophany for a subordinate angel, leaving unsaid whether divine-thron

items.label: M8
items.outcome: the guards shake and become as dead men
items.paraphrase: The guards, terrified of him, tremble and go slack like corpses.
items.gloss: The armed watchers, meant to guard the grave, are undone by what they see — the ones posted to keep order become the first to fall before it.
items.sitz: armed watchers overcome at an angelophany

items.label: M9
items.outcome: an address is delivered to them (contents in M10–M17)
items.paraphrase: The angel speaks to the women in reply.
items.gloss: Heaven now speaks to the women directly; where the guards were struck dumb, these witnesses are addressed.
items.sitz: an angelic messenger addressing mortal witnesses

items.label: M10
items.outcome: a prohibition of fear is issued to them
items.paraphrase: He tells them not to be afraid.
items.gloss: The old reassurance formula lifts fear off the women so they can receive what comes next; the immediate care is for their steadiness.
items.sitz: the standard 'do not fear' opening of an angelic address

items.label: M11
items.substrate: the women's purpose — that they are seeking the crucified Jesus
items.outcome: their errand is named and acknowledged
items.paraphrase: He states that he knows they are looking for the crucified Jesus.
items.gloss: The messenger names their errand before they say it — a small sign that what they came for is already known and held from above.
items.sitz: a heavenly messenger displaying knowledge of the visitors' motive

items.label: M12
items.outcome: not-stated
items.paraphrase: He announces that Jesus is not in the tomb.
items.gloss: The claim that changes everything is put first as an absence — heaven's own herald, not the women's inference, declares the tomb empty.
items.sitz: declaration at the empty grave

items.label: M13
items.outcome: Jesus is risen
items.paraphrase: He announces that Jesus has been raised, as Jesus foretold.
items.gloss: The empty tomb is now given its meaning: he has been raised, and Jesus' earlier word is what makes sense of what they are seeing.
items.sitz: proclamation that the crucified one has been raised, matching his prior word

items.label: M14
items.outcome: they are directed to inspect the empty resting-spot
items.paraphrase: He invites them to come and look at the place where Jesus' body had lain.
items.gloss: The women are invited to look for themselves; heaven's word does not ask them to bypass their eyes but to bring their eyes along.
items.sitz: an on-site invitation to verify the empty grave

items.label: M15
items.substrate: the women (as messengers to the disciples)
items.outcome: they are commissioned to carry the news
items.paraphrase: He orders them to go quickly and pass the news to the disciples.
items.gloss: Having received the news, they are turned outward — the encounter is not to be kept but carried, and quickly.
items.sitz: delegation of the announcement to human bearers

items.label: M16
items.agent: the angel (as author of the message the women are to speak)
items.substrate: the disciples (as addressees of the relayed message)
items.outcome: a message is composed for delivery: risen, going ahead to Galilee, will be seen there
items.paraphrase: The message they are to relay: that he has risen from the dead and is going ahead of them to Galilee, where they will see him.
items.gloss: The message they carry is not only that he is risen but that a meeting is set: the followers will see him where they first knew him.
items.sitz: a Galilee-rendezvous promise attached to the resurrection news

items.label: M17
items.outcome: the angel's telling is placed on record
items.paraphrase: He seals the address by noting that he has now delivered the message to them.
items.gloss: The messenger closes by vouching for his own words, so what the women carry rests on heaven's warrant, not on their memory of it.
items.sitz: a messenger closing his speech by warranting that he has spoken

items.label: M18
items.outcome: they are away from the tomb, carrying fear and great joy
items.paraphrase: The two women leave the tomb in a hurry, mixed with fear and great joy.
items.gloss: They leave carrying two feelings at once — dread and gladness — because what they've met is too big to fit into one.
items.sitz: eyewitness-report of departure from a numinous grave

items.label: M19
items.substrate: the news (the message they are commissioned to bring)
items.outcome: they are en route to the disciples with word
items.paraphrase: They run to carry the news to the disciples.
items.gloss: The running itself is the shape of the errand — obedience takes the form of hurry.
items.sitz: commissioned messengers hurrying to their addressees

items.label: M20
items.outcome: an encounter between Jesus and the women takes place
items.paraphrase: Jesus intercepts them on the way.
items.gloss: The one they were told about meets them face to face on the road, closing the distance between announcement and person — no angel stands between.
items.sitz: an unexpected appearance of the risen one to his messengers

items.label: M21
items.outcome: a greeting-command to rejoice is delivered
items.paraphrase: He greets them with a call to be glad.
items.gloss: He opens with an everyday greeting turned inside out — the ordinary word for 'rejoice' now comes from a mouth that has passed through death.
items.sitz: conventional joy-greeting turned into a resurrection-address

items.label: M22
items.outcome: they are grasping his feet
items.paraphrase: They approach him and clasp his feet.
items.gloss: They take hold of his feet — the risen one is not vapor; a body can be clasped, and they clasp it.
items.sitz: physical contact with the risen one, confirming his bodily presence

items.label: M23
items.outcome: worship is given to him
items.paraphrase: They render worship to him.
items.gloss: Touch tips over into worship: recognizing who he is, they render what belongs only to God.
items.sitz: prostrating reverence before a numinous figure

items.label: M24
items.outcome: an address is delivered to them (contents in M8–M10)
items.paraphrase: Jesus then speaks to them.
items.gloss: He now speaks to them himself — the earlier angelic word is repeated, this time by the one it was about.
items.sitz: the risen one addressing his first witnesses

items.label: M25
items.outcome: a prohibition of fear is issued
items.paraphrase: He tells them not to be afraid.
items.gloss: The same lifting of fear that the angel gave is now spoken by him in person, so his own voice steadies them.
items.sitz: standard reassurance-formula from a numinous figure

items.label: M26
items.substrate: the women (as messengers to his brothers)
items.outcome: they are sent to tell his brothers
items.paraphrase: He commissions them to carry word to his brothers.
items.gloss: He calls his followers 'brothers' and sends the women to them — the errand from heaven is reissued from him, with the household language intact.
items.sitz: the risen one deputizing the women as bearers of the news to his followers

items.label: M27
items.agent: Jesus (as author of the message to be relayed)
items.outcome: a directive-plus-promise is composed: go to Galilee, where they will see him
items.paraphrase: The content of the message: that the brothers are to head to Galilee and will see him there.
items.gloss: He confirms the rendezvous the angel named — Galilee is the appointed meeting-place, and his own mouth now seals it.
items.sitz: a Galilee-rendezvous promise attached to a going-order

items.label: M28
items.outcome: the guards arrive in the city
items.paraphrase: Meanwhile, some of the guards enter the city.
items.gloss: The scene shifts to ordinary human traffic — routed watchers walking back into the city, no heavenly light on them.
items.sitz: defeated watchers returning to the authorities that posted them

items.label: M29
items.outcome: the chief priests receive a full account of what occurred at the tomb
items.paraphrase: They report to the chief priests everything that had happened.
items.gloss: The guards tell the truth of what they saw — for one moment, even hostile witnesses carry the empty-tomb report to those in charge.
items.sitz: eyewitnesses debriefing the priestly authorities

items.label: M30
items.agent: the chief priests together with the elders
items.outcome: a plan is arrived at in council
items.paraphrase: The priests convene with the elders and confer.
items.gloss: The authorities close ranks; the news is treated as a threat to be managed rather than a claim to be tested, and the bond between them becomes a plotter's bond.
items.sitz: a Jerusalem authority-body deliberating over an unwelcome report

items.label: M31
items.outcome: the soldiers are paid off
items.paraphrase: They hand over a large sum of silver to the soldiers.
items.gloss: Silence is purchased with silver — the truth is not disputed, only bought off.
items.sitz: authorities buying compliance from the returning watchers

items.label: M32
items.outcome: an instruction is delivered (contents in M16–M17)
items.paraphrase: They speak to the soldiers, instructing them.
items.gloss: Speech becomes a tool of instruction from above: the guards will not be asked what happened, they will be told what to say.
items.sitz: authorities dictating a cover-story to their paid witnesses

items.label: M33
items.substrate: the soldiers (as future speakers of the account)
items.outcome: the soldiers are ordered to circulate a fabricated version
items.paraphrase: They direct the soldiers to give out a particular account.
items.gloss: A public story is authored to displace the one the guards actually lived — deception is put in place of testimony.
items.sitz: orchestrating a public counter-story to the empty-tomb report

items.label: M34
items.agent: Jesus' disciples (as posited actors in the story the soldiers are to tell)
items.outcome: a claim is composed: the disciples came by night and stole him while the guards slept
items.narrator: anonymous chronicler quoting the authorities' dictated line
items.paraphrase: The content the soldiers are to circulate: that Jesus' disciples came at night and stole his body while the guards were asleep.
items.gloss: The manufactured line — that the disciples stole the body while the guards slept — undoes itself on the surface (sleepers cannot vouch for what they slept through), and the teller lets that show.
items.sitz: a night-theft cover-story assigned to sleeping guards

items.label: M35
items.substrate: the governor (as one to be talked around) and the soldiers (as those being reassured)
items.outcome: a pledge is issued that the authorities will handle the governor and keep the soldiers out of trouble
items.paraphrase: The authorities keep instructing the soldiers: if word of this reaches the governor, they will smooth it over with him.
items.gloss: The authorities extend their cover backward into Roman power — they will absorb the risk so their scripted witnesses keep to the script.
items.sitz: Jerusalem authorities managing the risk that Roman power hears of the empty tomb

items.label: M36
items.outcome: the soldiers are in possession of the payment
items.paraphrase: The soldiers accept the silver.
items.gloss: The guards close the bargain by taking the money — testimony is now a paid service.
items.sitz: paid witnesses accepting a bribe

items.label: M37
items.outcome: the dictated cover-story is put into circulation
items.paraphrase: The soldiers carry out the instructions they were given.
items.gloss: They do as they were told — the lie is not just bought but actively spread.
items.sitz: paid witnesses performing the assigned script

items.label: M38
items.outcome: the story is current among Jews and remains so at the time of the telling
items.narrator: anonymous chronicler, aware of his own present
items.paraphrase: That account spreads widely among the Jews and is still in circulation at the time of the telling.
items.gloss: The counter-story outlives the moment and is still in the air at the time of writing — the teller acknowledges he is writing into a live dispute, not a settled one.
items.sitz: a late-first-century teller pointing out that this counter-story is still around in his day

items.label: M39
items.outcome: the eleven arrive at the appointed mountain
items.paraphrase: The eleven disciples travel to Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them to meet him.
items.gloss: The scene returns from the cover-up in the city to the followers keeping the appointment — obedience simply shows up where it was told to.
items.sitz: the followers keeping a rendezvous set by their teacher

lineage.seam: Is the text standing on the Torah mountain-commissioning pattern (Sinai/Horeb) here, and if so does the Galilean mountain claim continuity w

items.label: M40
items.outcome: the eleven catch sight of him
items.paraphrase: They see him.
items.gloss: The promise made twice becomes sight: with their own eyes, the followers meet him where he said they would.
items.sitz: followers first sighting the risen teacher at the appointed place

items.label: M41
items.outcome: reverence is rendered to him
items.paraphrase: They bow down before him.
items.gloss: Seeing turns at once into bowing — the appropriate response to who this is, not just relief that he is here.
items.sitz: followers prostrating before the risen one

items.label: M42
items.substrate: the sight of Jesus (as the object of their uncertainty)
items.outcome: a divided response is present — some doubt alongside the worship
items.paraphrase: Some of them, however, wavered in belief.
items.gloss: The teller refuses to tidy the moment — even at the sighting, some hesitate, and worship and wavering stand together in the same crowd.
items.sitz: a candid note that not every follower is settled in belief at the sighting

items.label: M43
items.outcome: Jesus is with them
items.paraphrase: Jesus approaches them.
items.gloss: He does not wait for their doubt to settle — he closes the gap himself, meeting the uncertain as well as the sure.
items.sitz: the risen one closing the distance to his followers

items.label: M44
items.outcome: an address is delivered (contents in M11–M16)
items.paraphrase: He addresses them.
items.gloss: He speaks to them all together — the parting words of the account are about to be given.
items.sitz: the risen one giving a final address to his followers on the mountain

items.label: M45
items.substrate: authority in heaven and on earth
items.outcome: Jesus stands as the one to whom all such authority has been given
items.paraphrase: He states that total authority in heaven and on earth has been handed to him.
items.gloss: Before anything is asked of them, he names his warrant: everything that follows rests on an authority he has been granted, not on their strength.
items.sitz: the risen one declaring his cosmic warrant before commissioning his followers

lineage.seam: imports the Danielic 'one like a son of man' investiture — universal dominion given by the Ancient of Days — as the warrant for the risen Je

items.label: M46
items.outcome: the eleven are dispatched
items.paraphrase: He orders them to go.
items.gloss: The mountain is not a resting place but a launch — the appointed meeting becomes a sending.
items.sitz: a sending-out on the authority just declared

items.label: M47
items.agent: the eleven (as the ones commanded to act)
items.outcome: a mandate that all peoples be turned into disciples
items.paraphrase: He orders them to make disciples of every nation.
items.gloss: The reach of the errand widens past Israel to all nations — the movement's addressee is now the whole world.
items.sitz: expanding the addressees of the movement beyond Israel

lineage.seam: Is the text standing on the Abrahamic 'all nations' promise here, and if so does 'make disciples of all nations' fulfill the blessing-to-the

items.label: M48
items.substrate: those made disciples of every nation
items.outcome: the discipled are to be initiated by baptism in the triune name
items.paraphrase: He orders them to baptize those they disciple in the threefold name — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
items.gloss: New disciples are to be marked in a threefold name — the God they enter into is named as Father, Son, and Spirit, and that naming is the door.
items.sitz: a threefold naming as the initiation-formula

items.label: M49
items.outcome: the discipled are to be trained to keep the whole of what he commanded
items.paraphrase: He orders them to teach the discipled to keep everything he has commanded.
items.gloss: Initiation is not the finish line — those brought in are to be shaped over time to keep everything he taught.
items.sitz: continuing formation attached to the initiation-command

items.label: M50
items.substrate: the eleven (and, by extension, those who continue the mission)
items.outcome: an abiding presence is pledged, lasting until the end of the age
items.paraphrase: He promises he will be with them continually, all the way to the age's end.
items.gloss: The final word is not departure but presence — he promises to stay with them, so the errand is carried under a companionship that outlasts the scene.
items.sitz: a closing promise of ongoing presence beyond the parting scene

reception.title: The resurrection end-silence — how it was received

readers.label: Lake
readers.reading: Lake treats the women's silence as the deliberate, emphatic main point of Mark's ending, while allowing that a now-lost continuation likely explained how they eventually spoke.
readers.quoted_span: the deliberate silence of the women at the beginning — which is the main point — is perfectly plain, for the statement is quite emphatic

readers.label: Orr (1908)
readers.reading: Orr acknowledges Mark breaks off at the women's flight in trembling, but insists Mark's Gospel nonetheless implied — no less than the others — that a report followed.
readers.quoted_span: St. Mark breaks off with the women fleeing from the tomb in "trembling and astonishment" ; but there can be no reasonable doubt that his Gospel also, not less than the others, contemplated a report of t

readers.label: Mark · ICC
readers.reading: Gould normalizes the abrupt ending as consistent with Mark's habitual brevity at the gospel's margins — not strange, not requiring explanation, simply characteristic.
readers.quoted_span: Mark gives merely the announcement of the resurrection to the women by the angels, and closes with this. This, instead of being strange, and requiring explanation, is quite in accordance with the character of Mark

readers.label: Matthew · ICC
readers.reading: Allen reads Mark's silence as naturally inviting a follow-up appearance; Matthew, uneasy with it, rewrites the women as speaking, then continues with the appearance — but unmotivated.
readers.quoted_span: It is very natural that this should have been followed by an appearance to them of Christ dispelling their fear and repeating the angel's message. Mt. alters "and told no one," etc., into "ran to tell His disciples."

readers.label: Longer Ending (16:9–20)
readers.reading: The most consequential reception act: a later hand SUPPLIED an ending — appearances + commission + ascension — precisely because Mark's abrupt 16:8 silence was felt as a gap that had to be closed.

readers.label: Shorter Ending
readers.reading: A second, briefer supplied ending in some manuscripts — independent evidence that the 16:8 silence generated MULTIPLE closure-attempts, not one.

readers.label: Narrative criticism
readers.reading: Reads 16:8 not as a defect or accident but as an INTENTIONAL narrative choice — the silence forces the reader to supply the continuation (the 'hermeneutic of secrecy'). NOT in our corpus (the narrative-critical register is a known coverage gap, IRR228) — added as attested/inferred.

center.label: Mark 16:8 — the end-silence
center.reading: Each account ends on a silence; Mark breaks off abruptly with the women afraid and saying nothing. What happens after is unnarrated, later supplied, or left open — the meaty end-gap.
center.title: The resurrection end-silence (Mark 16:8 · the unnarrated after)

cross_gospel.seam: comparative beats key on narrative beat + carried_by gospel; no verse or move handle joins a beat to the reader's selection. Method seam item (SS E requirement (a)/(b), SS I).
cross_gospel.seam_reader: the four gospels are lined up by episode, not verse by verse, so an episode cannot yet be matched to the verse you are reading.

beats.beat: female follower(s) travel to the tomb early on the first day
beats.note: MATT names two Marys; MARK three women with spices; LUKE a group with spices; JOHN Mary Magdalene alone

beats.beat: the sealing stone is found/made displaced from the tomb entrance
beats.note: MATT dramatizes an angel rolling it in real time; MARK/LUKE/JOHN find it already moved (divine passive)

beats.beat: the women/witness(es) enter or peer into the tomb
beats.note: MARK and LUKE enter bodily; JOHN has the disciples enter and Mary bend down to look; MATT omits an interior entry

beats.beat: the body of Jesus is discovered absent from its burial place
beats.note: framed as angelic declaration in MATT/MARK/LUKE and as empirical discovery-then-report in JOHN

beats.beat: one or more numinous figures (angel/young man/two men) are present at the tomb
beats.note: MATT one angel outside; MARK one young man inside; LUKE and JOHN two figures; JOHN's appear only in Mary's second visit

beats.beat: the numinous figure(s) are visually marked by whiteness/dazzling appearance
beats.note: lightning/snow (MATT), white robe (MARK), dazzling clothes (LUKE), white (JOHN)

beats.beat: the witnesses react with fear, dread, or bewilderment
beats.note: MATT guards struck down + women's mingled fear/joy; MARK alarm/terror; LUKE terror + bowing; JOHN grief rather than terror

beats.beat: the figure(s) address the witnesses with a speech-act interpreting the empty tomb
beats.note: MATT/MARK a commission; LUKE a rhetorical rebuke + reminder; JOHN only a 'why do you weep' question

beats.beat: the sought one is identified as the crucified Jesus
beats.note: MATT/MARK by the angelic naming, LUKE embedded in the passion-prediction; JOHN never verbalizes crucifixion in this scene

beats.beat: his absence from the tomb is explicitly declared ('he is not here')
beats.note: formulaic in the synoptics; JOHN dramatizes absence but never states the formula

beats.beat: his resurrected/raised status is announced (typically as divine passive)
beats.note: MATT/MARK/LUKE via the figures' proclamation; JOHN gestures at it only through the beloved disciple's belief and a scriptural aside

beats.beat: the witnesses are invited to view/verify the vacated burial spot
beats.note: MATT/MARK by directive ('come, see'); LUKE by finding no body; JOHN by inspection of the linen wrappings

beats.beat: a prior word of Jesus is invoked to frame what has happened
beats.note: MATT/MARK cite his earlier promise about Galilee; LUKE cites the passion-and-resurrection prediction; JOHN cites scripture instead

beats.beat: the witnesses depart from the tomb
beats.note: MATT hasten with fear+joy; MARK flee in terror; LUKE return to the eleven; JOHN Mary runs to Peter, disciples return home

beats.beat: the witnesses are commissioned/moved to report to the (male) disciples
beats.note: explicit commission in MATT/MARK; LUKE self-initiated report; JOHN Mary's spontaneous run to Peter/beloved disciple

beats.beat: the announcement is (or is to be) carried to Peter and the wider disciple circle
beats.note: MARK names Peter in the commission (and shorter ending); LUKE the eleven; JOHN Peter and the beloved disciple; MATT names 'his disciples' without Peter

beats.beat: a promise of future seeing/reunion with the risen Jesus is issued
beats.note: both locate it in Galilee via a 'he goes before you' formula; absent from LUKE and JOHN's tomb scene

beats.beat: male disciple(s) go to the tomb to verify the women's report
beats.note: LUKE Peter alone; JOHN Peter with the beloved disciple in a footrace

beats.beat: the linen burial cloths are seen lying in the tomb
beats.note: LUKE a single mention by Peter; JOHN elaborated as wrappings plus separately rolled head-cloth

beats.beat: a closing cognitive/affective state is left unresolved into full belief
beats.note: MARK women's fearful silence; LUKE Peter's amazement; contrast JOHN's beloved-disciple belief and MATT's commissioned joy

reliability.disposition: Reliability for this reading: not established. 2 of 12 engines has been measured, and no acceptance threshold has been declared — so the measurement cannot yield a verdict.
reliability.why_no_number: A number with no acceptance criterion cannot produce a verdict, and drawing it beside a claim will read as one. Repetition is evidence that runs happened, not that they agreed; agreement between runs is evidence about the instrument's stability, not about whether the reading is right. And the runs behind those figures were not independent of one another: the coder held a single conversation across passages, which is the one thing an agreement statistic assumes it does not. Declaring a threshold would not settle this — the figure is not awaiting a criterion, it is measuring something other than what it names.
